hero.title: File:Kalemie Medal Parade (12235622173).jpg
hero.description:
The Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General in the D. R. Congo, Martin Kobler, on his arrival in Kalemie, Katanga province, to officiate a medal parade ceremony organized by the Beninese contingent of MONUSCO Force. Next to the SRSG is the ambassador of Benin to the D. R. Congo who also travelled to the area to witness the event. Photo: MONUSCO/Myriam Asmani

Le Représentant spécial du Secrétaire général de l’ONU en R.D. Congo, Martin Kobler, à son arrivée à Kalémie, province du Katanga, pour présider une cérémonie de remise de médaille organisée par le contingent béninois de la Force de la MONUSCO. Le Représentant spécial avait à ses côtés l’ambassadrice du Benin en R. D. Congo, elle aussi ayant fait le déplacement pour être témoin de l’événement. Photo : MONUSCO/Myriam Asmani.

gallery.title: File:Galette.jpg
gallery.description: Back to Lake Tanganyika. Congo has its load of layered history, however it wouldn't be inaccurate to argue that Belgium, the foremost colonizer of this country, hasn't left significant traces in the nation's cuisine, when speaking about the eastern part. The administrative language being French doesnot reveal much of the past-days horror, and it's rather remixed with Swahili in a very pleasant way. So here is that yet-remaining, genuine lonely piece of Belgium, enacted in a dry margarine-saturated waffle eaten on the street. It's named Galette, and is sold everywhere, though quality varies.
categories: Cuisine of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

gallery.title: File:Matumgulupoli.jpg
gallery.description: Back to Lake Tanganyika. In Marché-Katanga I meet Justin (you should pronounce it the French way) by the matumgulupoli sailswoman's mat, and he is delighted to introduce this wild-growing bush fruit to me. He fissions the hard shell to expose the white flesh adorned with black seeds and sprinkles on it a pinch of wonderful pink mixture of piri piri and crystalline salt (from the wooden vial below his right hand). I keep questioning that bizarr fruit and he keeps insisting that "...no one grows this. It's the good Lord that gives us this aliment in the wild wood".
categories: Cuisine of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Nature of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

gallery.title: File:Menu 02.jpg
gallery.description: Back to Lake Tanganyika. A mixture of French and Swahili - with lovable spelling errors made in both - demonstrated in this large wall-menu at a traditional mama's restaurant on the main street. Ugali and fish, fish and beans or beef with cooked greenies and rice, whatever dish I ordered, I stroked it with heaps of pungent piri-piri paste. Prices are normally quoted in Congolese franc, however, your U.S. dollars are kindly accepted as well - though only in banknotes of later series.
categories: Cuisine of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

gallery.title: File:Piri piri.jpg
gallery.description: Back to Lake Tanganyika. A flushed exciting bunch of red hot peppers that here and in South Africa are called Piripiri and have a strong association to both the cuisine of Portugal and African cuisine. They are found in vast use in the local food culture and are as inspiring as they look.The greenish foreigner at the side of the pile is a mango, eaten with salt and piri piri.

gallery.title: File:Yogurt.jpg
gallery.description: Back to Lake Tanganyika. Here in Kalemie it's "You-gourt", so whenever I used the continental French's "Yaourt" I was little understood. This natural product is produced from fresh milk of Tanganyika cows - grazing only along the shores of the lake in Congo, Tanzania and Burundi and said to be milk-rich comparing with the cattle in the western parts of Congo, where people don't consume fresh milk - according to the owner of this specialized shop/restaurant in Quartier Dav. The guy in the picture is a client like me.

gallery.description: Kalemie, Katanga province, DR Congo : Celebration of the International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples, commemorated annually on 9 August. Theme of the day: “Post 2015 Agenda; Ensuring indigenous peoples’ health and well-being”. The celebration taking place at Lukwangulo camp for internally displaced indigenous people, focused on cultural values promotion, awareness-raising to combat HIV/AIDS and awareness-raising for road safety.

gallery.filename: Ici à Kalemie, province du Katanga, le 26 novembre 2014, Martin Kobler, épingle la médaille des Nations Unies sur la poitrine d’un soldat du contingent pakistanais (15554587193).jpg
gallery.title: File:Ici à Kalemie, province du Katanga, le 26 novembre 2014, Martin Kobler, épingle la médaille des Nations Unies sur la poitrine d’un soldat du contingent pakistanais (15554587193).jpg
gallery.description:
LEGENDE:  Dans son message de fin d’année adressé au personnel de la Mission le Chef de la MONUSCO remerciait le personnel en ces termes:  "Merci pour 2014. Durant ces derniers jours, pendant que je jetais un regard rétrospectif sur notre parcours commun en examinant nos accomplissements, j'ai ressenti une vague de fierté - fierté par rapport à nos succès et à vos contributions exceptionnelles.  Votre travail a été de qualité remarquable et a eu un impact considérable dans la poursuite des objectifs de la Mission. Je voudrais saisir cette occasion pour vous remercier pour votre appui, votre dévouement ainsi que pour votre volonté résolue à aller plus loin et ceci en dépit des conditions souvent très difficiles. »  Ici à Kalemie, province du Katanga, le 26 novembre 2014, Martin Kobler, épingle la médaille des Nations Unies sur la poitrine d’un soldat du contingent pakistanais, soldat auquel tout le personnel de la mission peut s’identifier, fier qu’il est de contribuer à la consolidation de la paix en RDC.  Photo MONUSCO/Abel Kavanagh 
CAPTION:  In his end-of-year message to the Mission’s staff, the Head of MONUSCO thanked the staff in these terms:

“Thank you for 2014.  Over the last few days, as I reflected on our common journey and considered our achievements, I felt a surge of pride - pride over our successes and your exceptional contributions. As we are coming to the end of the year, I must say that we have achieved quite a lot together. The quality of your work has been outstanding and has had a huge impact on pursuing the goals of the Mission. I would like to take this opportunity to thank you for your support and dedication and for going the extra mile, often under very difficult conditions, ”. Here in Kalemie, Katanga province, on 26 November 2014, Martin Kobler pins the UN medal on a soldier of the Pakistani contingent, a soldier with whom all Mission staff can identify, proud as he is to be contributing to peace building in DRC. Photo MONUSCO/Abel Kavanagh

gallery.title: File:Une famille congolaise cultivant les champs dans les environs de Kalemie (15363000350).jpg
gallery.description:
LEGENDE : « L’agriculture familiale joue un rôle vital dans la société congolaise » a déclaré Martin Kobler, Représentant spécial du Secrétaire général de l’ONU en RDC, à l’occasion de  la Journée Mondiale de la l’Alimentation célébrée ce 16 octobre 2014. 
La photo montre une famille cultivant son champ dans les environs de la ville de Kalemie, dans la province du Katanga. Photo MONUSCO/ Myriam Asmani

==
CAPTION : “Family agriculture plays a vital role in Congolese society,” declared Martin Kobler, Special Representative of the United Nations Secretary-General in the DRC, on the occasion of the World Food Day, celebrated on 16 October. 

The photo shows a Congolese family cultivating its field on the outskirts of the town of Kalemie, Katanga province. Photo MONUSCO/Myriam Asmani

gallery.title: File:Renforcement la capacité de la PNC, pendant une formation de court durée sur la police technique scientifique (PTS) (15466637605).jpg
gallery.description:
LEGENDE :  Kalemie, Nord Katanga, RD Congo, 29 sept. 2014 : Un formateur de la Police MONUSCO (UNPOL),  Nabil Al-Mossabi, effectuant une démonstration des procédures de levée de corps sur une scène de crime.  C’était dans le cadre d’une formation  sur  le travail de police technique et scientifique sur les scènes de crime, dispensée à l’intention d’officiers de police judiciaire de la PNC. Photo MONUSCO/Capitain Zied Hamrouni. 

=
CAPTION : Kalemie, North Katanga, DR Congo, 29 Sept. 2014: A trainer from MONUSCO Police (UNPOL), Nabil Al-Mossabi, performing a demonstration of the procedures for the recovery of a body from a crime scene. This was part of a training session on technical and forensic police work on crime scenes provided to judicial police officers of the PNC. Photo MONUSCO/Captain Zied Hamrouni
